processes.title: Retirement & Decommission
processes.summary: Sunset what the portfolio decided to retire: move users, keep or dispose of data lawfully, and switch off for good.

definition.purpose: Retire products, features, components and tools deliberately, so users are moved, data is handled lawfully and cost and risk really go away.
definition.outcome: A retirement plan (RET-##), users transitioned, a verified data disposition, and a decommission record with savings and lessons.
definition.jtbd: When we decide to stop something, help us switch it off cleanly — without stranding anyone or losing data we must keep.
entry: Portfolio decision to retire, or a retire slice of a modernisation
exit: Data disposed per the retention schedule and certified

normal: Retain, migrate or dispose of data
flow.stateTransitions: Decided → Planned → Notified → Data disposed → Read-only → Off → Closed

cases.happyPath: Few dependants, replacement live, simple data, quiet scream test.
exceptions: Hidden user found in the scream test → move them, extend read-only
failures: Zombie system still running and costing

routing.forward: Decommission record → 8.4 Portfolio Review and the learning log; the cycle closes
routing.alternate: Partial retirement → feature removed through PLAN
routing.rework: Dependant without a path or reconciliation failure → re-plan / re-migrate
routing.escalation: Legal hold, date change or shared platform → legal / sponsor / platform owner
routing.stop: Replacement cannot serve users → retirement stopped; back to 8.4 — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Every data class disposed per rule and verified
rules: Read-only before off; off before removal
Never delete records under retention or legal hold

principles: Keep only the data you must

decisions: Can it be switched off, and is it gone?

agents: AI assistants for dependency discovery and drafting notices
roles: C — Data owner, Legal, Privacy officer, Security, Vendor manager
execution.authority: Service owner signs off; data owner approves disposition; privacy officer signs personal-data disposal; legal rules on holds; sponsor approves date changes.

continuity.handoff: Decommission record & savings → 8.4 Portfolio Review; lessons → learning log; the cycle closes
traceability: Creates RET-##; decommission record and certificates link RET-## and PDC-###

learning: Hidden dependants and data surprises — learning log

lessons.prompt:
I'm working through "Plan the Retirement" (Evolve → Retirement & Decommission) on my own project. Act as my assistant: draft and check, I decide.

Goal: Retire on purpose, with nothing and no one left behind.
Done looks like: An approved retirement plan (RET-##) with dependants, replacement paths, data classes, timeline and proof of switch-off.

I'll attach or paste: Portfolio decision record; Service inventory; Retention schedule.

Work through these steps with me, one at a time:
1. Confirm scope from the decision
2. Map dependants → Dependency map
3. Classify data vs retention schedule → Data inventory & disposition
4. Draft timeline & replacement paths → Sunset plan
5. Approved by service owner, data owner & sponsor? (a decision — give me the options and a recommendation; I make the call)

Produce: Retirement plan. Use clear headings I can paste into my document.

Before you finish, check it against: Every dependant in the inventory addressed; Every data class mapped to a rule; Every dependant addressed; Every data class mapped.

Ask me for anything you need instead of guessing. Keep it specific to my project.

definition.purpose: Move every user and consumer off before anything is switched off.

exit: Every dependant at 100% moved, or an owned exception

lessons.title: Retain, Migrate or Dispose of Data
lessons.summary: Apply the retention schedule: migrate, archive or securely delete each class of data, with evidence.

definition.purpose: Keep what must be kept, move what is still needed and delete the rest — provably.
definition.outcome: A data disposition record with every class done and verified, and deletion or archive certificates filed.
definition.jtbd: Help me be sure we kept what the law requires and deleted what we must.
entry: Users transitioned or migration window open
exit: Every data class disposed per its rule and verified

normal: Migrate needed data to the successor and reconcile
Securely delete the rest, including copies and backups

cases.happyPath: Clean classes, a simple migration and verified deletion.
alternates: Data needed by the successor → migrate with reconciliation
edgeCases: Personal data in unexpected places (exports, spreadsheets)
Backups that cannot be deleted selectively → expire on schedule
exceptions: Legal hold arrives mid-disposal → pause that class

routing.alternate: Backups cannot be purged → document their expiry date
routing.escalation: Legal hold or regulator query → legal / privacy officer
routing.stop: Disposal unlawful or unsafe → stop that class and record — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Every class has rule, disposition and verifier
Personal data with no basis deleted
checks: A second person verifies each disposition
rules: Never delete records under retention or legal hold
Deletion covers copies, exports and backups
policies: Privacy officer signs off personal-data disposal

principles: Keep only the data you must

roles: C — Records manager, Privacy officer, Legal
execution.authority: Data owner approves each disposition; the privacy officer signs personal-data disposal; legal rules on holds.

continuity.handoff: Data disposition record & certificates → 8.5.4 Decommission & Close

lessons.title: Decommission & Close
lessons.summary: Go read-only, scream-test, switch off, remove everything and close with savings and lessons.

definition.purpose: Make sure it is really gone — and its cost and risk with it.
definition.outcome: A decommission record: switched off; infrastructure, access, integrations, monitoring and licences removed; inventory updated; savings and lessons recorded.
definition.jtbd: Help me close this for good and prove it.

normal: Remove infrastructure, access, integrations, monitoring and licences
Update the inventory and records of processing
Record savings and lessons; sign off
parallel: Removal tasks run concurrently after switch-off

alternates: Scream test finds a user → move them and extend read-only
exceptions: Rollback needed during read-only → restore and re-plan
failures: 'Switched off' but still running and costing

routing.forward: Decommission record → 8.4 Portfolio Review (savings) and the learning log; the cycle closes
routing.alternate: Scream test finds users → extend read-only and move them
routing.escalation: Removal touches a shared platform → platform owner
routing.stop: Decommission aborted → restore and record why — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Zero use for the scream-test period
rules: Read-only before off; off before removal

roles: C — Security, Finance partner, Platform owner
execution.authority: Service owner signs off; the operations lead verifies; the platform owner approves shared-infrastructure changes.

continuity.handoff: Decommission record → 8.4 Portfolio Review; learning log → next cycle
traceability: Decommission record closes RET-##; LRN-### links it

workflows.title: Switch Off & Close
workflows.summary: Go read-only and scream-test, switch off, remove every trace — infrastructure, access, integrations, monitoring, licences — then record savings and lessons.

lenses.note: Read-only first; log every attempted use.
Quiet for the whole period before switching off.
Accounts, keys and credentials revoked on the day.
Infrastructure, DNS and certificates removed.
Monitoring and alerts removed.
Savings reported to finance.
Inventory shows Retired.

loops: Users found → move them, extend read-only
